subject: Accounting
name: Accounting, Units 3 and 4
about: VCE, Recording, reporting, budgeting and decisions
syllabus: VCE Accounting Study Design (from 2025), Units 3 and 4

units.title: Unit 3: Financial accounting for a trading business

points.title: Qualitative characteristics
points.brief: Useful financial information is relevant and a faithful representation, and is better when comparable, verifiable, timely and understandable.

points.title: Assumptions of accounting
points.brief: Records rest on assumptions such as the entity, going concern, period, accrual basis and monetary unit, which set what is recorded and when.

points.title: Elements of financial reports
points.brief: Assets, liabilities, owner's equity, revenue and expenses, each defined so items can be classified, and assets and liabilities split into current and non-current.

points.title: Ethical considerations
points.brief: Decisions should consider honesty in reporting, fair treatment of staff and suppliers, and effects on the environment and community.

points.title: Double entry accounting
points.brief: Every transaction is recorded with at least one debit and one credit of equal value, so the ledger stays in balance.

points.title: Debit and credit rules
points.brief: Assets and expenses increase with a debit. Liabilities, owner's equity and revenue increase with a credit.

points.title: The general journal
points.brief: The journal for every transaction in Unit 3, from cash and credit trading to returns, drawings, stock used for advertising, assets the owner contributes and corrections.

points.title: The general ledger
points.brief: The ledger holds a T-form account for each item. Journal entries are posted to it, and each account shows its running balance.

points.title: Recording GST
points.brief: GST collected and paid is recorded in a GST Clearing account, whose balance shows what the business owes the tax office or is owed back.

points.title: The trial balance
points.brief: A list of every ledger balance that checks total debits equal total credits. It does not catch every error.

points.title: Inventory in the ledger
points.brief: With a perpetual system, FIFO or identified cost inventory cards back up the ledger, and write-downs and stock losses are recorded in both.

points.title: Product and period costs
points.brief: Costs to get goods ready for sale, such as freight in, are product costs added to inventory. Other costs are period costs, expensed as they occur.

points.title: Lower of cost and net realisable value
points.brief: Inventory is reported at the lower of its cost and what it can be sold for less selling costs. A fall below cost is written down.

points.title: Allowance for doubtful debts
points.brief: At the end of the period, an estimate of debts that will not be collected is recorded as an expense and an allowance against accounts receivable.

points.title: Writing off bad debts
points.brief: In the next period, a debt that will not be paid is written off against the allowance, not as a new expense.

points.title: Turnover indicators
points.brief: Inventory turnover, accounts receivable turnover and accounts payable turnover show how many days stock sits, customers take to pay and the business takes to pay.

points.title: Managing inventory and credit
points.brief: Internal controls, non-financial information and strategies such as tighter credit terms or better stock control improve how a trading business runs.

points.title: Balancing the ledger
points.brief: At the end of the period, asset, liability and owner's equity accounts are balanced and their balances carried forward.

points.title: Closing entries
points.brief: Revenue and expense accounts are closed to a Profit and Loss Summary account, then profit and drawings are transferred to the owner's capital.

points.title: The income statement
points.brief: A report of revenue less expenses over a period, from gross profit through to net profit.

points.title: The balance sheet
points.brief: A report of assets, liabilities and owner's equity at a date, each split into current and non-current.

points.title: The cash flow statement
points.brief: A report of cash in and out, grouped into operating, investing and financing activities.

points.title: Classifying cash flows
points.brief: Paying wages is operating, buying equipment is investing, and a loan or capital contribution is financing.

points.title: Cash and profit compared
points.brief: A business can make a profit and still run short of cash, because timing of cash differs from when revenue and expenses are recorded.

units.title: Unit 4: Recording, reporting, budgeting and decision-making

points.title: Buying a non-current asset
points.brief: An asset bought for cash or with a loan is recorded at cost, and a loan adds a liability that is repaid over time.

points.title: Depreciation adjustments
points.brief: Each period's depreciation, straight-line or reducing balance, is recorded as an expense and added to accumulated depreciation against the asset.

points.title: Depreciation methods compared
points.brief: The method chosen changes each year's profit and the carrying amount on the balance sheet, though not the total depreciated.

points.title: Disposing of a non-current asset
points.brief: Selling an asset for more or less than its carrying amount records a gain or loss. GST applies to a cash sale but not to a trade-in.

points.title: Why adjustments are made
points.brief: At the end of the period, adjustments make sure revenue and expenses belong to the period they relate to.

points.title: Prepaid expenses
points.brief: An expense paid in advance is recorded as an asset, then moved to an expense as it is used up.

points.title: Accrued expenses
points.brief: An expense used but not paid yet, such as wages owing, is recorded as an expense and a liability, then cleared when paid next period.

points.title: Accrued revenue
points.brief: Revenue earned but not received yet is recorded as revenue and an asset, then cleared when the cash arrives next period.

points.title: Unearned revenue
points.brief: A deposit received before goods or services are provided is a liability until the revenue is earned.

points.title: The adjusted trial balance
points.brief: A trial balance prepared after balance day adjustments, used to prepare the end-of-period reports.

points.title: Why businesses budget
points.brief: Budgets plan future results, set targets, warn of cash shortfalls and give a basis to compare actual results.

points.title: The budgeted cash flow statement
points.brief: An estimate of cash in and out by activity, which shows whether the business will have enough cash.

points.title: The budgeted income statement
points.brief: An estimate of revenue and expenses for the coming period, built on the accrual basis.

points.title: The budgeted balance sheet
points.brief: An estimate of assets, liabilities and owner's equity at the end of the coming period.

points.title: Variance reports
points.brief: Comparing budgeted and actual figures, and trends over several periods, shows favourable and unfavourable variances to explain.

points.title: Profitability
points.brief: Profitability is how well a business makes profit compared to its sales, assets and the owner's investment.

points.title: Profitability ratios
points.brief: Return on owner's investment, return on assets, net profit margin and gross profit margin each compare profit with something else.

points.title: Liquidity
points.brief: Liquidity is the ability to pay debts as they fall due, measured by the working capital ratio and the quick asset ratio.

points.title: Efficiency ratios
points.brief: Asset turnover, inventory turnover, days receivable and days payable show how well the business uses its resources.

points.title: Non-financial information
points.brief: Customer satisfaction, staff turnover, product quality and reputation help explain the numbers and guide decisions.

points.title: Comparing performance
points.brief: Ratios mean most compared with past results, the budget and similar businesses, but differences in methods, timing and one-off events limit what they show.

points.title: Strategies to improve performance
points.brief: Raising prices, cutting costs, managing inventory, collecting debts faster and selling idle assets can lift profit or cash.
